newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate climbs on pre-election jitters.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate climbs on pre-election jitters.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up a sharp 125 basis points in late morning trade on Monday due to market nerves ahead of the forthcoming U.S. Federal Open Market Commitee meeting and national mid-term elections, dealers and analysts said.

"The market is under great pressure and I think it will be all week. That was to be expected, with elections (on July 6) and the FOMC meeting (Tuesday and Wednesday) coming up," a fixed-income analyst said.
Dealers said month-end demand for liquidity was also exerting upside pressure on rates.
Mexico will hold mid-term elections on July 6 to renew the entire lower house of Congress, one-quarter of the Senate, six state governors and, for the first time in modern times, Mexico City mayor.
Dealers said they did not expect the FOMC to raise U.S. interest rates, but it nonetheless added to uncertainty in a skittish market.
"This is a difficult and nervous week. We don't expect the FOMC to raise U.S. rates, but that has happened on occasions when the market has been at its most confident," a dealer said.
Overnight rates on bank paper had meanwhile risen 20 basis points to 25.50 percent.
Liquidity of 4.713 billion pesos was due to return to the system during the session from prior central bank operations.
